claim: An LLM that sees scored past attempts (OPRO-style) finds optima on small search problems but degrades fast with size; at TSP n=50 the gap is 11.0% for gpt-4, 133-220% for weaker models, versus 9.8% for farthest insertion. Independent replication: Huang et al. 2024 found the same size trend (GPT-4 gap 0.00% at n=10, 3.38% at n=25, 11.01% at n=30); OPT-Engine 2026 finds a size cliff for text-only reasoning in DeepSeek V3.2 and GPT-5.1.
agent_test: Same token budget: scored-history proposal loop vs plain best-of-N on 10-, 20- and 50-option selection tasks with a code-computed score; plot gap by size.
audit_note: OPT-Engine concerns optimization modeling with chain-of-thought, a looser analogue of OPRO-style; numbers match OPRO Table 3 and Huang Table II.

claim: Model strength is a dominant factor in LLM-as-optimizer quality: gpt-4 reached the TSP optimum in 9.6 steps at n=10 vs 40-47 for weaker models, and text-bison got 0/5 successes at n=15.
agent_test: Run the S7 select loop with a weak and a strong backbone at equal tokens; check whether the loop gain shrinks with the weak one.

claim: LLM-written genetic operators (selection, crossover, mutation) beat just asking the LLM for new solutions: LMEA gap 3.94% vs OPRO 26.30% at rue-20 and 18.72% vs 53.59% at rue-25, yet still worse than classic heuristics (1.4-2.3%) at 25 nodes.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare 'propose one improved answer' vs 'recombine two candidate answers then select' on a fixed option-set task.

claim: A raise-temperature-when-stuck rule is a useful explore/exploit dial: LMEA self-adaptation cut rue-20 gap from 11.82% to 3.94%; OPRO default temperature 1.0 beat 0.0 and 0.5 in prompt optimization.
agent_test: Add a stall detector that raises sampling temperature or forces a new framing after k non-improving rounds; compare with fixed temperature at equal tokens.
audit_note: Two sources on different tasks, both support their halves.

claim: A zero-shot LLM as offspring operator in MOEA/D matches a GA operator on RE21-RE25 (2 LLM wins, 2 GA wins, 1 tie), so on synthetic or smooth benchmarks the LLM adds no clear gain over classic operators.
agent_test: Treat 'LLM adds value' as untested on easy tasks; always run a cheap non-LLM baseline at equal tokens.

claim: No search method wins everywhere: on ZDT/UF benchmarks MOEA/D-DE wins the hard UF problems, NSGA-II wins some, the LLM-distilled linear operator is robust but rarely best; on ZDT4 MOEA/D-DE collapsed to HV 0.301 vs 0.721.
agent_test: Keep a portfolio of 2-3 selection strategies and test a router vs always using one, on mixed task types.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In low-budget, expensive-evaluation hardware design spaces, LLM-guided exploration with domain rules reaches Pareto quality with far fewer evaluations than NSGA-II, MOEA/D, ACO, GA or BO (iDSE 16.6x ADRS vs NSGA-II and matches NSGA-II at 4.6% of designs; Lumina 6 designs beat A100 in 20 steps; MicroEvo +36.22% HV at budget 20; driving agent 6 vs 0 Pareto points in 15 iterations). All are author-run, none independently replicated. Counter-evidence (2026): against tuned classical optimisers (CMA-ES, TPE, SMAC) frontier LLM agents lose at a 24-hour budget; the low-budget LLM edge is vs random and default baselines (10 evaluations, d04) and does not carry over.
agent_test: Replicate on our tasks: scorer-checked candidate pool, LLM-picks-with-rules vs random pick at 20 evaluations.

claim: LLM gain in design-space search is tied to domain knowledge in the prompt in several systems: iDSE domain-knowledge injection added a further 45.0% effectiveness; Lumina rules lifted Qwen-3 perf/area accuracy 0.59 to 0.82; MPM-LLM4DSE used a pragma-impact prompt. In LLEMA the full system (memory, multi-island evolution, chemistry rules) reached hit rate 30.2 vs 4.4 for a plain LLM, but unguided mutation+crossover already reached 29.8, so rules add little to hit rate there. A rules-only (no LLM) control is still missing. In iDSE all baselines shared the same rule pruning, so pruning alone is not the lead.
agent_test: Ablate S7 with and without a short human-written list of domain failure rules in the prompt, at equal tokens.
audit_note: LLEMA 4.4 to 30.2 is plain LLM vs the full system (memory, multi-island evolution, surrogate, chemistry rules); the unguided mutation+crossover variant already reaches 29.8, so rules/memory alone do not explain it.
claim_before_audit: The LLM gain in design-space search depends on domain knowledge injected into the prompt: iDSE domain-knowledge step added 45.0% effectiveness; Lumina rules lifted Qwen-3 perf/area accuracy 0.59 to 0.82; LLEMA chemistry rules plus memory raised hit rate from 4.4 to 30.2; MPM-LLM4DSE used a pragma-impact prompt. Rules-only (no LLM) control is still missing everywhere. In iDSE all baselines shared the same rule pruning, so pruning alone is not the lead.

claim: LLMs make recurring, nameable errors when judging trade-offs: changing many parameters at once, computing deltas against the wrong baseline, ignoring negative side-effects; forcing one change at a time fixed them in Lumina. Unaided trade-off (parameter tuning) accuracy was only 0.26 to 0.40 for three open LLMs, 0.46 to 0.63 with rules.
agent_test: Add a rule 'one change per candidate, state the baseline' and measure error rate of trade-off judgments on a labelled set.

claim: Warm-starting search with good seeds helps on average: LLM seed designs beat Latin hypercube, beta and random start in iDSE (NSGA-II warm start 3.17x geo-mean ADRS gain over random start, 2.3x over LHS; MOEA/D 3.41x), but warm start was far worse on one benchmark (autocorr 0.7458 vs 0.0883). LLAMBO warm start gives less diverse points than random. No paper links this diversity loss to final Pareto spread.
agent_test: Compare diverse-first generation vs LLM-best-guess seeding at equal tokens, and track diversity (the LLAMBO caveat).
audit_note: 'No paper links diversity loss to Pareto spread' is an absence claim limited to the researcher's search; iDSE Table 3 numbers (3.17x, 3.41x, 0.7458 vs 0.0883) and LLAMBO lower generalized variance verified.

claim: Evolving both an idea in words and the code is far more query-efficient than evolving code alone: EoH reached 0.993 fitness in about 2,000 LLM queries vs about 1 million for FunSearch on bin packing; heuristics can fail out of distribution (FunSearch 6.75% vs best fit 4.50% at capacity 500).
agent_test: Candidates carry a one-line rationale plus answer; compare with answer-only candidates at equal tokens, and test on a shifted distribution.

claim: Selection on a measured multi-objective score is the norm in successful LLM design-search work (HV, IGD, ADRS computed by code), while LLMs rating options by opinion are too generous and too uniform (materials study: MAE about 3 of 10 vs 136 experts, low spread).
agent_test: Compare LLM-judged trade-off ranking against computed Pareto ranking on tasks with ground truth; use computed filter first, LLM judge only on ties.
audit_note: The 'norm' statement rests on the researcher's own tally of opened papers, not an external survey; materials numbers (136 experts, MAE~3, z>0, SD 2.49 vs 3.35) match.

claim: Hypervolume is the standard single-number quality indicator of a trade-off set; cheap in 2-3 objectives (O(n log n)) but exact contribution is #P-hard and subset selection NP-hard for d>=3; Pareto dominance loses selection pressure beyond about four objectives.
agent_test: Limit active criteria in a select step to 3-4 or aggregate them; test selection quality as criteria count rises from 2 to 8.

claim: Constraint handling by dominance (feasible beats infeasible; smaller violation wins) needs no penalty weights and is a clean rule for a select step.
agent_test: Apply 'feasibility first, then compare' ordering in S7 vs a weighted-sum score at equal tokens.

claim: Combining LLM mutation with non-dominated sorting and a verified checker gives correct and Pareto-good results (POET 40/40 correct vs 29/40 I/O prompting); LLM-evolved MOBO matched qParEGO at about 60x lower wall-clock but fell in the same Friedman top group.
agent_test: Pareto-rank candidates and keep only verifier-passing ones; compare with single-score ranking at equal tokens.

claim: Plain Bayesian optimization's reputation for failing in high dimensions is mostly an artifact of kernel and initialization (standard GP with Matern kernel or robust length-scale init works to d=600), so weak baselines can inflate LLM-method gains. Independent confirmation of the weak-baseline concern: tuned classical methods beat frontier LLM agents on autoresearch HPO (d01), and a plain (1+1) elitist loop was competitive with FunSearch, EoH and ReEvo (d05).
agent_test: Tune the non-LLM baseline equally; report gain only against the tuned baseline.
audit_note: Xu: Matern works to d=600 (init 1.0); Ferreira: classical beats LLM agents in fixed space; Zhang: (1+1) baseline competitive except on OBP Weibull.

claim: Prompt-based optimization overfits and is sensitive to meta-prompt order, score display and temperature (training accuracy exceeds test by 5-20%).
agent_test: Select on one item set, evaluate on held-out items; randomize candidate order.

claim: A chosen subset of tools beat the full toolset in an agentic Pareto explorer (AutoCircuit, log-hypervolume up to 2.4x over LLM-only), and fine-tuning with simulator feedback widens the Pareto front (e-SimFT HV 0.621 vs 0.573). Both only seen in abstract or partial text.
agent_test: c19 needs training so is out of scope; for c16 compare minimal vs full tool menu at equal tokens.

claim: On a one-task HPO benchmark with 3 seeds and a 24-hour budget, tuned classical optimisers (TPE 0.9768, SMAC 0.9778, CMA-ES 0.9785) beat the best pure LLM agent (0.9814 with code editing), and a hybrid where CMA-ES state is shared with an LLM that proposes a minority of trials is best (0.9763; 0.8B model r=0.1 gives 0.9744; r=0.8 degrades to 0.9849).
agent_test: Run S7 with a code-held score table and a minority (10-50%) of LLM-proposed candidates vs an LLM-only loop; compare at equal evaluations.

claim: The size cliff of LLM-as-optimizer persists in 2025-26 reasoning models: text-only reasoning degrades with problem size (DeepSeek V3.2, GPT-5.1), the model drops to nearest-neighbour and cheapest-insertion heuristics near the cliff, and delegating to solver code keeps accuracy; on CO-Bench the best one-shot LLM (Claude-3.7 Sonnet 0.65) stays below the classical solver (0.797), while agent search (FunSearch 0.842) exceeds it.
agent_test: Compare LLM picks among 10, 20, 50 options with and without a code scorer and enumerator; locate the cliff for the current backbone.

claim: Simple search loops are hard to beat: a plain (1+1) elitist LLM loop is competitive with FunSearch, EoH and ReEvo except on one of four problems; seeding it with known good algorithms gives best average rank in 5 of 6 settings; BestOfN matched or beat some complex agents in CO-Bench.
agent_test: Use best-of-N with a code scorer as the control and add structure only when it beats it at equal tokens.

claim: An LLM that chooses among options in one pass is weaker than a staged procedure whose aggregation is done in code: DeLLMa (state forecast, pairwise utility ranking, expected utility in code) reaches 73.3% vs 33.3% for o1-preview zero-shot on agriculture and 64.2% vs 35.0% on stocks, with gains larger for larger action sets, at similar cost.
agent_test: Compare one-pass 'pick the best' to pairwise scoring plus code aggregation on a labelled set of 3, 6, 10 options at equal tokens.

claim: LLM judges are unreliable exactly where selection is hard, among near-equal options: position bias is strongest when the quality gap is small (15 judges, over 150,000 instances), pairwise preferences are non-transitive with the share rising from about 3% to about 40% as items get closer, and a panel of 9 frontier judges holds about 2 independent votes (MNLI panel 72.0% vs best judge 71.8%).
agent_test: Shuffle option order and aggregate across passes; measure self-agreement across orderings as a confidence signal.
audit_note: Non-transitive share figures are read from chart bin labels (2.64 to 40.21).

claim: Set-based design with LLM agents has a working template (tools score utility and CVaR risk, agents prune 100 to 64 to 50 designs, human picks the last) but no study yet compares it to non-LLM pruning or to human designers.
agent_test: Implement staged narrowing with code filters and compare with one-shot choice.

claim: NSGA-II (2002): convergence better than PAES and SPEA on all but ZDT3 and ZDT6 (PAES; paper also credits SPEA on ZDT6), diversity best on all nine, 25,000 evaluations, 10 runs, NSGA-II left untuned; the constrained-domination rule needs no penalty parameter; many-objective behaviour is untested in the paper.
agent_test: Use feasible-beats-infeasible then non-dominated rank then spread as the tie-break order in code.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors
